results.title: Steps taken to promote Women Entrepreneur
results.content: Read MBA, BBA, B.COM Notes. In India, promoting women entrepreneurship has become a priority for both the government and various organizations. Launched in 2016, the Stand-Up India Scheme aims to provide financial support to women and SC/ST entrepreneurs. The scheme also includes support for business planning and mentorship. The Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) Scheme provides financial assistance to micro and small enterprises, including those led by women. This scheme is designed to support women entrepreneurs in setting up small-scale industries. It includes training programs, workshops, and access to credit facilities to help women start and grow their businesses. Institutions such as the National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) and state-level EDIs provide specialized training programs for women entrepreneurs. Organizations like the **Federation of Indian Women Entrepreneurs (FIWE)** and the **National Association of Women Entrepreneurs of India (NAWEI)** offer platforms for women to network, share experiences, and access resources.
